newsitem.title: THAILAND: Hemraj in Thailand land sale talks with GM.
newsitem.headline: Hemraj in Thailand land sale talks with GM.

text.p: Thai property firm Hemraj Land Development Plc said on Thursday it was negotiating sale of land to General Motors Corp on which the U.S. auto giant may build its proposed $750 million assembly plant.
"Negotiations will be finalised in about one week. We have high potential to win the GM land purchase," its managing director Prateep Trilohaka told Reuters.

GM was discussing the purchase of about 300 rai (57 hectares) of land in Hemraj's industrial park in the eastern seaboard in Rayong province, Prateep added. He declined to give the value of the proposed land deal.
GM officials in Thailand were not available to confirm the talks or give any further details.
The U.S. auto-maker announced late in May that it would build its new regional manufacturing facility in Thailand, after looking at a possible site in Philippines.
The plant was initially expected to produce 80,000-100,000 Opel Astra cars mainly for export to the regional market, it said then.
Hemraj's competitor in the land deal is Siam Cement Plc, which has land at its industrial park, also in Rayong.
